text: Hi, I’m Antoni. I had a small Polish prototype before the hackathon. Everything you’ll see here was built during it, on Meta’s Muse models.
ph: Haj, ajm AN-to-ni. Aj hed e smoł POU-lisz PROU-to-tajp bi-FOR dhe HE-ka-thon. EW-ri-thing jul si hir łoz bilt DJUR-ing it, on ME-tez MIUZ MO-dlz.

text: Some conversations you only get one shot at. A pitch. A thesis defence. A salary talk. A cold call.
ph: Sam kon-wer-SEJ-szyns ju ON-li get łan szot et. E pitsz. E THI-sis di-FENS. E SE-le-ri tok. E kołd kol.

text: Forty billion is the whole pie. What is your monthly revenue?
ph: FOR-ti BIL-ien iz dhe houl paj. Łot iz jor MAN-thli RE-we-niu?

text: I have two minutes. Why should I give you a raise?
ph: Aj hew tu MI-nets. Łaj szud aj giw ju e rejz?

text: Honestly, why would I trust you with this?
ph: O-nest-li, łaj łud aj trast ju łidh dhis?

text: And nobody wants to be your sparring partner at midnight. So I built one.
ph: End NO-bo-di łonts tu bi jor SPA-ring PART-ner et MID-najt. Sou aj bilt łan.

text: Sparing Live. You call them. They listen, they interrupt you, they read your shared screen, and their face shows their mood. They can hang up. And afterwards, a reviewer shows you what they were privately thinking.
ph: SPA-ring lajw. Ju kol dhem. Dhej LI-sn, dhej in-te-RAPT ju, dhej rid jor szerd skrin, end dher fejs szołz dher mud. Dhej ken heng ap. End AF-ter-łerdz, e ri-WJU-er szołz ju łot dhej łer PRAJ-wet-li THIN-king.

text: This is not a chat window. It is a full-duplex voice loop with barge-in, specialised agents, and a hidden state you only see in the review.
ph: Dhis iz not e czet ŁIN-dou. It iz e ful DJU-pleks wojs lup łidh BARDŻ-in, SPE-szy-lajzd EJ-dżents, end e HI-dn stejt ju ON-li si in dhe ri-WJU.

text: This is the real app. I press Demo, it fills in a call to a seed-stage investor, and I place the call. In this recording I typed my side, with the sound off. With a headset, you just talk.
ph: Dhis iz dhe ril ep. Aj pres DE-mou, it filz in e kol tu e sid-stejdż in-WES-tor, end aj plejs dhe kol. In dhis ri-KOR-ding aj tajpt maj sajd, łidh dhe saund of. Łidh e HED-set, ju dżast tok.

text: She answers in about a second, on Muse Spark Open, served by Baseten.
ph: Szi AN-serz in e-BAUT e SE-kend, on miuz spark OU-pen, serwd baj BEJ-sten.

text: She goes straight for my weakest line: the market size, with no customers behind it.
ph: Szi gouz strejt for maj WI-kest lajn: dhe MAR-kit sajz, łidh nou KAS-te-merz bi-HAJND it.

text: Then I give her real numbers: three paying customers, two renewals. Her mood turns, and she agrees to a second meeting.
ph: Dhen aj giw her ril NAM-berz: thri PEJ-ing KAS-te-merz, tu ri-NIU-elz. Her mud ternz, end szi e-GRIZ tu e SE-kend MI-ting.

text: When I hang up, Muse Wonder reviews the call. A score, her attitude over time, and what to fix next.
ph: Łen aj heng ap, miuz ŁAN-der ri-WJUZ dhe kol. E skor, her E-ti-tjud OU-wer tajm, end łot tu fiks nekst.

text: And the app shows which Meta model ran each step of this exact call, straight from its own budget ledger.
ph: End dhe ep szołz łicz ME-te MO-dl ren icz step ow dhis ig-ZEKT kol, strejt from itz oun BA-dżit LE-dżer.

text: The replay puts her private thoughts next to my words, so I can see the exact sentence where I lost her.
ph: Dhe ri-PLEJ puts her PRAJ-wet thots nekst tu maj łerdz, sou aj ken si dhi ig-ZEKT SEN-tens łer aj lost her.

text: Under the hood, Voice Transcribe hears me, Muse Spark Open plays the character, Wonder researches the company and writes the review, and Muse Image draws the face. On the same scripted calls, open weights answered in about a second. Hosted Spark took two and a half, the day I measured. No failed turns. No repeats.
ph: AN-der dhe hud, wojs tran-SKRAJB hirz mi, miuz spark OU-pen plejz dhe KE-rik-ter, ŁAN-der ri-SER-czyz dhe KAM-pe-ni end rajts dhe ri-WJU, end miuz I-midż drołz dhe fejs. On dhe sejm SKRIP-ted kolz, OU-pen łejts AN-serd in e-BAUT e SE-kend. HOU-sted spark tuk tu end e haf, dhe dej aj ME-żerd. Nou fejld ternz. Nou ri-PITS.

text: It runs in English and Polish, it is open source under MIT, and the repo has run instructions for Windows, Mac and Linux. Thanks for watching.
ph: It ranz in IN-glisz end POU-lisz, it iz OU-pen sors AN-der em aj TI, end dhe RI-pou hez ran in-STRAK-szyns for ŁIN-douz, mek end LI-naks. Thenks for ŁO-czing.
